---
title: Introduction
description: Semantic canonicalizer for Tailwind CSS — rewrite utilities only when provably equivalent.
---

**tailwind-canonicalize** is a production-grade CLI and library that rewrites Tailwind utility classes into their theme-canonical form — **only when the result is provably identical**.

It is **not** a linter and **not** a general formatter. It sits beside Biome, ESLint, Oxlint, and Prettier without fighting them.

```tsx
// before
<div className="w-[40px] min-w-[10rem] h-[10px] p-[16px] gap-[8px]" />

// after
<div className="w-10 min-w-40 h-2.5 p-4 gap-2" />
```

```package-install
pnpm add -D tailwind-canonicalize
```

```bash
pnpm exec tailwind-canonicalize . --write --safe
pnpm exec tailwind-canonicalize . --check
```

## Three transformation categories

| Category | What | Safety |
|----------|------|--------|
| **Canonical class** | Arbitrary values → theme tokens | Automatic when exact |
| **Tailwind migration** | e.g. `bg-gradient-to-br` → `bg-linear-to-br` | Versioned registry |
| **Semantic tokens** | `bg-white` → `bg-background` | Analyze + **approved** manifest only |

## Goals

### Zero false positives

Unknown values, `calc()`, `var()`, and multi-match ambiguity are **never** rewritten. Coverage is secondary to safety.

### Theme-driven

Loads project `@theme` (v4) or `tailwind.config.*` (v3). Never hardcodes your design system.

### Format-preserving

Uses MagicString and a real AST (oxc). Comments, multiline class strings, and non-class code stay intact.

### Ecosystem-friendly

[First-class integration guides](/docs/integrations) for Biome, ESLint, Oxlint, Prettier, and CI.

title: API

```ts
import {
  canonicalizeClass,
  canonicalizeClasses,
  canonicalizeFile,
  canonicalizeProject,
  canonicalizeSource,
  findCanonicalEquivalent,
  defineConfig,
  createDefaultTheme,
  loadProjectTheme,
  createTailwindCompileEqual,
  watchProject,
} from "tailwind-canonicalize";
```

## findCanonicalEquivalent

```ts
const match = findCanonicalEquivalent("w-[40px]");
// { canonical: "w-10", reason: "theme-exact", ... } | null
```

## canonicalizeClass / canonicalizeClasses

```ts
canonicalizeClass("w-[40px]"); // "w-10"
canonicalizeClasses(["w-[40px]", "flex"]); // ["w-10", "flex"]
```

## canonicalizeSource

```ts
const result = canonicalizeSource(source, {
  filePath: "Card.tsx",
  migrations: true,
});
// { code, changed, transformations, diagnostics }
```

## canonicalizeProject

```ts
const summary = await canonicalizeProject({
  paths: ["src"],
  write: true,
  mode: "safe",
  incremental: true,
  workers: "auto",
});
```

## Theme loading

```ts
const { theme, source } = await loadProjectTheme(process.cwd());
// source: "css" | "v3-config" | "default"
```

## defineConfig

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "tailwind-canonicalize";

export default defineConfig({
  tailwind: { version: 4 },
  canonicalize: { arbitraryValues: true },
});
```

## Transformation records

Every rewrite includes:

```ts
{
  category: "canonical-class" | "tailwind-migration" | "semantic-color-token" | ...,
  original: string,
  replacement: string,
  confidence: "exact" | "high" | "medium" | "low",
  safety: "safe" | "review" | "aggressive",
  token?: string,
  file?: string,
  line?: number,
}
```

/docs/architecture.mdx:
---
title: Architecture
description: Package layers and transformation pipeline.
---

```text
Parser  →  Extract class candidates (oxc AST)
        →  Resolver (theme + candidates + compare)
        →  Migrations / tokens / recipes
        →  MagicString rewrite
        →  Print
```

## Packages

| Package | Role |
|---------|------|
| `@tailwind-canonicalize/parser` | AST extraction |
| `@tailwind-canonicalize/resolver` | Theme, migrations, pipeline |
| `@tailwind-canonicalize/tokens` | Semantic analyze / apply |
| `@tailwind-canonicalize/transformer` | MagicString |
| `@tailwind-canonicalize/compiler` | Project scan, workers, watch |
| `tailwind-canonicalize` | CLI |

## Pipeline order

1. Tailwind migrations  
2. Arbitrary canonicalization  
3. Recipe overrides  
4. Semantic mappings (approved / aggressive)  
5. Dark-pair collapse  
6. Duplicate removal  
7. Conflict diagnostics  

See monorepo `docs/architecture/` for deeper design notes.

## Usage

```bash
tailwind-canonicalize [paths...] [options]
tailwind-canonicalize tokens analyze [paths...] [--out manifest.json]
tailwind-canonicalize tokens apply <manifest.json> [paths...] [--write]
```

## Core options

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--write` | Write rewrites to disk |
| `--check` | Exit 1 if changes would be made |
| `--stdin` | Read source from stdin → stdout |
| `--json` | Machine-readable summary |
| `--verbose` | Categorized rewrite details |
| `--diff` | Line diffs |
| `--safe` | Exact/safe only (default mode) |
| `--review` | Report only; never write |
| `--aggressive` | Review-level migrations / high-confidence inference |

## Migrations

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--migrate` | Apply versioned class renames |
| `--migrations-only` | Skip arbitrary canonicalization |
| `--from-tailwind <n>` | Source major (e.g. 3) |
| `--to-tailwind <n>` | Target major (e.g. 4) |

## Performance

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--watch` | Watch mode (+ incremental) |
| `--incremental` | Hash cache skip |
| `--workers` | Force worker pool |
| `--concurrency <n>` | Parallelism (default 8) |

## Compile verification

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--strict-compile` | Require Tailwind compile equality |
| `--compile-css` | CSS entry for compiler |

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `0` | Success |
| `1` | Changes required (`--check`) |
| `2` | Error |

## Example output

```
✓ 1,523 files
✓ 9,421 replacements
✓ 0 unsafe rewrites
Completed in 1.82s
```

```bash

# review proposed.json → save as tailwind-tokens.json
```

---
title: FAQ
description: Common questions about tailwind-canonicalize.
---

### Is this a linter?

No. It rewrites Tailwind utilities when equivalence is proven. Use Biome/ESLint/Oxlint for lint.

### Will it break my design?

Only rewrites that match your theme (or approved token map) apply. Ambiguous cases are left alone.

### Does it sort classes?

No. Use prettier-plugin-tailwindcss or eslint-plugin-tailwindcss for ordering.

### Can it invent semantic tokens automatically?

Analyze proposes; **apply** requires an approved manifest. Default mode never auto-applies semantics.

### v3 and v4?

v4 `@theme` first. v3 `tailwind.config.*` is loaded when no CSS theme is found. Migrations cover common v3→v4 renames.

### Monorepo?

Yes — pass package paths, use `--workers`, and per-package scripts. Theme discovery uses project CSS/config near cwd.

---
title: Canonical classes
description: Arbitrary values rewritten to theme scale keys when exact.
---

## What rewrites

Spacing, sizing, radius, font size, keywords, fractions — with variants and `!` preserved.

```tsx
max-w-[160px]        → max-w-40
hover:md:w-[40px]!   → hover:md:w-10!
rounded-[8px]        → rounded-lg
text-[16px]          → text-base
```

## How equivalence works

1. Parse utility structure  
2. Resolve active theme (`@theme` or defaults)  
3. Normalize lengths (px ↔ rem at root 16)  
4. Match scale keys  
5. Require a single safe candidate  

Optional: `--strict-compile` uses Tailwind’s `compile()` API when installed.

/docs/features/tokens.mdx:
---
title: Semantic tokens
description: Two-phase palette → design-token migration.
---

Semantic replacements are **architectural**, not purely canonical. The same `bg-amber-200` may mean warning, selection, or decoration — so inference never auto-writes.

## Phase 1 — Analyze

```bash
pnpm exec tailwind-canonicalize tokens analyze . --out proposed.json
```

No source edits. Outputs proposals, conflicts, duplicate token reports, cycles.

## Phase 2 — Apply

```bash
pnpm exec tailwind-canonicalize tokens apply tailwind-tokens.json --write
```

Only explicit mappings, pairs, and recipes in the manifest.

## Dark pairs

```tsx
bg-white dark:bg-slate-950  →  bg-background
```

when the pair is approved and dual-theme values exist.

## Theme CSS

Generates Tailwind v4 `@theme` / `@theme inline` with optional `:root` + `.dark` app variables. Prefers aliasing existing `--warning-subtle` over inventing duplicates.

## Requirements

- Node.js **20+**
- ESM project (or consume the CLI as a binary)

## Install

```package-install
pnpm add -D tailwind-canonicalize
```

```bash
# npm
npm i -D tailwind-canonicalize

# yarn
yarn add -D tailwind-canonicalize
```

## First run

```bash
# Report only
pnpm exec tailwind-canonicalize . --check

# Apply safe rewrites
pnpm exec tailwind-canonicalize . --write --safe
```

## package.json scripts

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "canonicalize": "tailwind-canonicalize . --write --safe",
    "canonicalize:check": "tailwind-canonicalize . --check --json"
  }
}
```

## Optional peer: Tailwind compile verification

```package-install
pnpm add -D tailwindcss
```

```bash
pnpm exec tailwind-canonicalize . --strict-compile --write
```

## Config file (optional)

```ts
// tailwind-canonicalize.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from "tailwind-canonicalize";

export default defineConfig({
  tailwind: {
    version: 4,
    stylesheet: "./src/styles/globals.css",
  },
  canonicalize: {
    arbitraryValues: true,
    deprecatedClasses: true,
    duplicateClasses: true,
  },
  migrations: {
    gradients: true,
    tailwindV4: true,
  },
});
```

## Wire formatters

Canonicalize does **not** replace Biome/ESLint. See [Integrations](/docs/integrations).

/docs/safety.mdx:
---
title: Safety
description: Zero false positives — the core product contract.
---

## Contract

A rewrite is applied only when **exactly one** theme candidate matches after value normalization (or a registered migration / approved mapping applies).

| Situation | Behavior |
|-----------|----------|
| 0 candidates | Leave untouched |
| 1 candidate | Rewrite |
| \>1 candidates | Leave untouched (unless documented preference, e.g. `1/2` over `2/4`) |
| `calc` / `var` / `min` / `max` / `clamp` | Never |
| Arbitrary properties `[mask-image:…]` | Never |
| Semantic palette → token | Never without approved manifest |

## Modes

| Mode | Flag | Applies |
|------|------|---------|
| Safe | `--safe` (default) | Exact canonical + safe migrations + approved tokens + dups |
| Review | `--review` | Report/diff only |
| Aggressive | `--aggressive` | Explicit; may include review migrations / high-confidence inference |

## Idempotence

```bash
tailwind-canonicalize . --write
tailwind-canonicalize . --write   # zero changes
```

## Unsafe counter

CLI always reports `unsafe: 0` — the engine refuses ambiguous rewrites rather than guessing.

/docs/troubleshooting.mdx:
---
title: Troubleshooting
description: Fix common setup and rewrite issues.
---

### No rewrites happen

- Confirm classes are in supported positions (`className`, `clsx`, `cn`, …)
- Check theme load (`--verbose` or JSON `themeSource`)
- Values like `w-[13px]` have no scale match — intentional

### CI fails with exit 1

```bash
pnpm exec tailwind-canonicalize . --write --safe
# or inspect
pnpm exec tailwind-canonicalize . --check --verbose --diff
```

### Cache seems stale

Delete `.tailwind-canonicalize-cache.json` or change options (options hash invalidates).

### Conflicts with Biome/Prettier

Run canonicalize **then** format. Don’t enable two tools that rewrite the same class strings.

### Semantic tokens not applied

Ensure `tokens apply` + manifest path, or config `tokens.enabled` + `manifest`. Safe mode never invents mappings.
